fallen.title: You hear the word – but it is not the answer
fallen.why: An announcement often gives two numbers or two places. A wrong option uses exactly the word you heard. Listen for “not …”, “instead” and “now”.
fallen.wrong: “… it will now leave from platform 6, not **platform 3**.” – I heard 3, so the answer is platform 3.
fallen.right: “It will **now leave from platform 6**, not platform 3.” – The answer is platform 6.

task.context: Radio: “The library is closing early on Friday, at four o’clock instead of six. On Saturday it is open as usual, from nine until five.”
task.prompt: When does the library close on Friday?
task.fb: You hear “six” and “five” too – but on Friday it closes at four, “instead of six”.

fallen.wo: B1 skills mock · Reading, Part 4 – also ISE I · Reading, true or false
fallen.title: One small word makes the statement false
fallen.why: In true/false tasks the statement sounds almost like the text. Watch small words such as only, all, never, always, every. One of them is enough to make it false.
fallen.wrong: “A Standard member can use the gym at 6 pm.” – The gym is open until 10 pm, so true.
fallen.right: False: Standard members may use the gym **only between 9 am and 4 pm**. 6 pm is peak time, for Premium members.

task.context: House rules: “Bikes may be left in the hall only if they do not block the way to the stairs.”
task.prompt: “You can never leave a bike in the hall.”
task.fb: “never” is too strong: you can leave it there if it doesn’t block the stairs.

fallen.source: B1 skills mock, set 1, task 37 · ISE I practice set 1, Reading, questions 6–13

fallen.title: For one situation there is no advert
fallen.why: There are more situations than adverts that fit. If an advert matches only half of what the person needs, it is not the answer – choose “none”.
fallen.wrong: You want a dentist who is open on Saturdays. – There is a dentist advert, so I choose it.
fallen.right: Read the opening times: if no advert offers **Saturdays**, the answer is **none**.

task.context: Advert: “City Swimming Pool – lessons for adults, Monday to Friday evenings.”
task.prompt: You want swimming lessons on Sunday mornings. Does this advert fit?
task.fb: The pool has adult lessons, but only on weekday evenings – not on Sunday mornings.

fallen.title: The right text says it in other words
fallen.why: The question and the text rarely use the same words. Look for the same idea, not the same word: “help with the cost” can be “staff can claim money towards …”.
fallen.wrong: “Which text offers help with the cost of a season ticket?” – I look for the word **cost** and choose the text with “costs”.
fallen.right: Text C says staff “can **claim up to £20 a month towards** a season ticket” – that is help with the cost.

task.context: Text: “Members don’t pay anything for the first lesson.”
task.prompt: Does this text say the first lesson is free?
task.fb: “don’t pay anything” means the same as “free”.

fallen.source: ISE I practice set 1, Reading, question 21

fallen.title: The title fits the whole paragraph, not one sentence
fallen.why: A wrong title often matches one detail in the paragraph. Ask: what is the whole paragraph about? There is one extra title that fits no paragraph.
fallen.wrong: The paragraph mentions a van, so I choose the title about transport.
fallen.right: The paragraph is about **how the project began** – the van is only one detail.

task.context: Paragraph: “At first Sam fixed bikes alone in his garage. Then friends started to help, and after a year twenty people came every Saturday.”
task.fb: The garage and Saturday are details. The paragraph tells how the project grew.

fallen.source: ISE I practice set 1, Reading, questions 1–5

fallen.wo: B1 skills mock · Reading, Part 5 (gaps in a letter)
fallen.title: because, so that, although: check the meaning first
fallen.why: All three words join two parts of a sentence. Only the meaning decides: a reason (because), a purpose (so that) or a contrast (although).
fallen.wrong: “I have turned off the water **because** nothing worse happens.” – because sounds fine.
fallen.right: “I have turned off the water **so that** nothing worse happens.” – the second part is the purpose.

task.context: “I left early ______ I could catch the first bus.”
task.fb: Catching the bus is the purpose of leaving early: so that.

fallen.wo: ISE I · Reading, Task 1 (complete the sentences)
fallen.title: Copy the exact words from the text
fallen.why: In sentence and note completion the answer is a number, word or phrase from the text – maximum three words. Don’t write it in your own words and don’t add extra words.
fallen.wrong: “Priya paid ____ for a van.” – I write **forty pounds for it**.
fallen.right: The text says “She paid **£40** for a van.” – write £40.

task.context: Text: “The café opened in a former bank in 2019.”
task.prompt: The café is in an old ____ . Which answer is best?
task.fb: Use the word from the text and keep it short: bank.

fallen.source: ISE I practice set 1, Reading, questions 14–18

fallen.wo: B1 skills mock · Reading, Part 5 (gaps in a letter)
fallen.title: last weekend, yesterday, ago: past simple, not present perfect
fallen.why: A finished time (last weekend, yesterday, two days ago) needs the past simple. The present perfect (has started) does not go with a finished time.
fallen.wrong: “A leak **has started** in my flat last weekend.”
fallen.right: “A leak **started** in my flat last weekend.”

task.fb: “two years ago” is a finished time: past simple, moved.

fallen.wo: B1 skills mock · Reading, Part 5 (gaps in a letter)
fallen.title: grateful for, interested in: the word chooses the preposition
fallen.why: Many adjectives and verbs always take the same preposition. Learn them as a pair: grateful for, interested in, good at, wait for.
fallen.wrong: “I would be very grateful **of** a quick reply.”
fallen.right: “I would be very grateful **for** a quick reply.”

fallen.title: Four points in the task – four points in your text
fallen.why: Examiners check every point. A beautiful text that forgets one point loses marks. Tick the points off before you finish.
fallen.wrong: I say yes and say when I can come – and stop. The key and my question are missing.
fallen.right: **Say yes · say when · say where the key is · ask a question** – one or two sentences for each.

task.context: Task: “Say yes. Say when you can come. Say where you will keep the key. Ask what else you need to know.”
task.prompt: A text says: “Of course I can feed your cat. I can come every morning at 7.30.” What is missing?
task.fb: Two of the four points are missing: where the key will be and a question.

fallen.source: B1 skills mock, set 1, writing task A

fallen.wo: B1 skills mock · Writing and Reading, Part 5
fallen.title: To a landlord or a company, write a formal letter
fallen.why: To a friend you can write “Hi Sam” and “See you!”. To a landlord, a shop or an office, use a formal greeting and ending, and polite requests.
fallen.wrong: “Hi Ms Berger, fix my sink pls! Bye”
fallen.right: “**Dear Ms Berger**, … **Could you please** send a plumber? … **Yours sincerely**, Folake Adeyemi”

task.context: You are writing to the manager of a hotel about a problem with your booking.
task.fb: A formal letter to someone you know by name ends with “Yours sincerely”.

fallen.source: B1 skills mock, set 1, Reading Part 5 (letter to the landlord) and writing task B

fallen.title: The conversation is not an interview: ask questions too
fallen.why: In the ISE I conversation the examiner wants to hear you ask for information and opinions, not only answer. A short question back keeps the conversation going.
fallen.wrong: Examiner: “Do you like travelling by train?” – “Yes.” (and silence)
fallen.right: “Yes, I do, because I can read on the way. **What about you – do you prefer the train or the car?**”

task.context: Examiner: “I went to Scotland last summer.”
task.prompt: Which answer keeps the conversation going best?
options: Really? What did you like most there?
task.answer: Really? What did you like most there?
task.fb: A follow-up question shows interest and uses the function “asking for information”.

fallen.source: ISE I practice set 1, Speaking, conversation task
